name: sheep

attributes.attribute: unlucky to meet in the early morning

sources: O’Sullivan, Patrick V. Irish Superstitions and Legends of Animals and Birds. Cork: Mercier, 1991, 80.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The sheep is an Irish folkloric animal. Sheep raising has fed the Irish economy for hundreds of years. Yet almost no myth features the sheep. Bulls and cows fill the old stories. The contrast is sharp. Sheep stay outside the mythic frame. A few folk beliefs touch them. To meet sheep early in the morning was unlucky. People thought it best to knit in the evening, when the sheep lay sleeping. The thin place of sheep in Irish story may reflect the wealth the cattle held. A land of cow and bull kept the sheep at hand and out of the tale.
